title: I-adically complete ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. The *$I$-adic completion* of $A$ is $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/I^n$ (the inverse limit of the quotient rings along the projections $A/I^{n+1}\to A/I^n$), with the canonical ring map $A\to A^\wedge$, $a\mapsto(a\bmod I^n)_n$. The ring $A$ is *$I$-adically complete* if this canonical map is bijective (hence a ring isomorphism); this includes the condition $\bigcap_nI^n=0$.
